fields.reasoning: Read the question, unstable-ci-guidance (acceptance pins the rule to review.md via TestReviewText 'unstable-ci'), review.md today (the rule sits beside the scoped-tests rule for checks, critics and fixers), Decision review-role-topics-shape and leaf review-guide (review becomes a short index; role topics carry the rules via shared blocks), leaf review-role-skills-installed (review.md's old phrases checked by review_test.go must be found in the role topics), and the fixer-topic, ci-fix-topic and gate-fix-topic leaves, whose acceptances already require the shared unstable-CI block expanded. The node is stale, not the plan: keeping the rule in the index would duplicate it and contradict the index shape already chosen, matching the rulings on the sibling findings (scoped-tests-in-role-topics, command-budget-in-role-topics). I weighed adding the block to the check and critic topics too, as was done for scoped tests, but the rule is about not pushing or rerunning CI to see a red; checks and critics never push or commit, and conflict-fix resolves merges rather than CI reds, so the three fixer topics are its natural and complete home. No CLI command, flag, --json shape, rhiza.* setting or .rhiza/ format changes, so no breaking note.
fields.statement: unstable-ci-guidance is updated in this change set to follow the split, not by keeping the rule in the review index: AGENTS.md and the rhiza-build topic keep the unstable-CI reproduce-locally rule unchanged (TestClaudeMDScopedTests and TestBuildText as today), and on the review side the rule lives in the shared unstable-CI block expanded into the fixer, ci-fix and gate-fix topics, the roles that fix a red and commit after it; the node's statement names those topics instead of rhiza-review, and its acceptance finds the rule in their texts through the guide package tests instead of TestReviewText on review.md.
